Advance Transfer Table

A manoeuvring aid providing predicted advance (distance along original track) and transfer (lateral distance) for specific speeds and rudder angles to plan safe turns.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Advance Transfer Table?

In this glossary, Advance Transfer Table refers to: A manoeuvring aid providing predicted advance (distance along original track) and transfer (lateral distance) for specific speeds and rudder angles to plan safe turns.

How is Advance Transfer Table used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Master: Consult the advance transfer table; we need 0.3 nm advance and 0.15 nm transfer for a 15-knot, 20-degree rudder turn."

Why does Advance Transfer Table matter in maritime?

Advance Transfer Table matters because it supports clear communication in Nav contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Advance Transfer Table?

Advance Transfer Table is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

What category does Advance Transfer Table belong to?

Where does this definition come from?

Definition

A manoeuvring aid providing predicted advance (distance along original track) and transfer (lateral distance) for specific speeds and rudder angles to plan safe turns.

Operational example

Master: Consult the advance transfer table; we need zero point three nautical miles advance and zero point one five transfer for a 15-knot, 20-degree rudder turn.
